h1: The open source vector database: free, self-hosted, Apache 2.0
sub: Milvus is a free, Apache 2.0 open source vector database from the LF AI & Data Foundation, written in Go and C++ for high-performance search at scale. Start with pip install, grow to tens of billions of vectors on Kubernetes, and keep the same API.
proof: Scales to tens of billions of vectors

benefits.title: Open source, for real
benefits.body: Apache 2.0 and governed by the LF AI & Data Foundation. Hundreds of contributors build it in the open on GitHub.

benefits.title: Fast on every CPU
benefits.body: The Knowhere engine picks SSE, AVX2, AVX512 or ARM instructions at runtime, and GPU indexes such as CAGRA run on NVIDIA hardware.

benefits.title: Scales out, not up
benefits.body: Storage and compute are separated. Stateless query, streaming and data nodes scale independently on Kubernetes, up to tens of billions of vectors.

benefits.title: Trusted in production
benefits.body: NVIDIA, Salesforce, Walmart, eBay, IBM and Reddit appear on the Milvus adopter wall. Meituan runs 10B+ vectors on self-hosted Milvus.

feature_blocks.title: An open ecosystem, not a walled garden
feature_blocks.body: Official SDKs and a REST API cover the common stacks; Milvus plugs into the AI tools you use.
bullets: SDKs for Python, Java, Go and Node.js, plus a RESTful API
Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, Hugging Face, Spark and Kafka
Attu GUI, Prometheus/Grafana monitoring and Milvus CDC for operations

feature_blocks.title: Every major index, one engine
feature_blocks.body: Choose the index per vector field for your recall, latency and memory budget, and combine vector search with filters or full-text search.
bullets: HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, SCANN and RaBitQ quantization (IVF_RABITQ)
BM25 full-text search and sparse vectors for hybrid search

feature_blocks.title: Built for billions and many tenants
feature_blocks.body: Distributed Milvus installs with the official Helm chart or Milvus Operator and keeps cost in check as data grows.
bullets: Add query nodes for reads and streaming or data nodes for writes
Hot/cold tiered storage keeps cold data on object storage
Up to 65,536 collections per cluster by default; partition keys serve millions of tenants

code.h2: Local vector database in Python: pip install to first search
code.intro: Milvus Lite ships with pymilvus. No server, no Docker, no account: the database is a local file.
code.code:
# pip install -U "pymilvus[milvus-lite]"
import random
from pymilvus import MilvusClient

client = MilvusClient("milvus_demo.db")  # Milvus Lite: data lives in this local file
client.create_collection(collection_name="demo", dimension=768)

docs = ["Milvus is an open-source vector database.", "It runs on a laptop or on Kubernetes."]
vecs = [[random.random() for _ in range(768)] for _ in docs]  # swap in your embedding model
client.insert(collection_name="demo",
              data=[{"id": i, "vector": v, "text": t} for i, (v, t) in enumerate(zip(vecs, docs))])

print(client.search(collection_name="demo", data=[vecs[0]], limit=2, output_fields=["text"]))
code.note: To move to a server, pass its URI (for example http://localhost:19530) to MilvusClient.

faqs: Yes. Apache 2.0 permits commercial use, modification and redistribution at no cost. You pay only for the infrastructure you run, or for Zilliz Cloud managed hosting.
Who maintains Milvus, and could the license change?
Milvus is a graduated LF AI & Data Foundation project with open governance; Zilliz is its major contributor. Released Apache 2.0 code stays Apache 2.0.
How does Milvus rank in an open source vector database comparison?
Use VectorDBBench, the open source benchmark that runs the same datasets on every database: on Cohere 1M, Milvus-16c64g-sq4u-fp16-force_merge reached 9,575.69 QPS at 2.3 ms P99.
Is it an open source vector database for RAG and LLM apps?
Yes. LangChain and LlamaIndex ship Milvus integrations, built-in BM25 gives hybrid search, and filters plus partition keys cover RAG and agent memory.
Is a self-hosted, on-premise vector database production-ready at scale?
Distributed Milvus runs on Kubernetes with replicas and independent scaling. Meituan runs 10B+ vectors on self-hosted Milvus; Read AI serves 20–50 ms retrieval to millions of users.

final.h2: Run an open source vector database in five minutes
final.body: pip install pymilvus, open a local file, and search. Move to Standalone or Kubernetes when data grows, or hand operations to Zilliz Cloud, no rewrite.
